title: The Chamber Where Water Becomes Stone's Student

features.name: stone-lectern
features.desc-on-touch: Carved smooth by water that has since stopped flowing. The stone reads like it's speaking, shaped by a voice that lasted millennia. Water pooled here to listen.

features.name: waterway-transcript
features.desc-on-touch: Marks on the chamber floor recording the water's passage: depth, speed, what it was carrying. The stone is reading and writing simultaneously, documenting the lesson.

features.name: erosion-as-pedagogy
features.desc-on-touch: The walls are carved with deliberate channels, but they're worn in unexpected ways—as if the water is teaching the stone that its lesson is different than it expected.

features.name: pool-of-stillness
features.desc-on-touch: A basin carved by water, now holding water that doesn't move. This is where the stream came to rest and think. The stone taught it patience.

features.name: question-carved-in-stone
features.desc-on-touch: A shape that might be writing, might be the trace of a tool, might be the stone asking something. The water paused here. Perhaps to answer.

inscription: where the student learns that the teacher had been learning all along

file.name: Water_Literacy_Chamber_Curriculum_Draft_Incomplete.txt
file.note: lesson plan written in stone: how to listen, how to shape without breaking, how to remember the one who shaped you. The stone is still learning to teach.

reverie.title: REVERIE — in the creek where the archive began
narr: You wade to the pool where she crouches, mapping the flow.
The stone here is smooth, worn by generations of water.
'Look how it's teaching itself,' she says, fingers on the curve.
You don't understand at first. Then you do—the water carved this
and the stone learned to keep shape, to hold the lesson.
'That's what we're building,' she says. 'A stone that learns.'
